topic: survey about video and multimodal generation

citation_audit.claim: A latent-diffusion line of work showed a practical route by pretraining image generators, then extending them into video generators with temporal modules and video fine-tuning [1].
citation_audit.evidence: The page states: "We first pre-train an LDM on images only; then, we turn the image generator into a video generator by introducing a temporal dimension to the latent space diffusion model and fine-tuning on encoded image sequences, i.e., videos." It also says they "insert temporal layers" and "fine-tune the model's decoder for video generation."

citation_audit.claim: The literature on controllable video generation has broadened the input space substantially.
citation_audit.evidence: The abstract says recent research has explored the integration of additional non-textual conditions, such as camera motion, depth maps, and human pose, to extend pretrained video generation models and enable more controllable video synthesis.

citation_audit.claim: VBench is important because it states that Inception Score, FID, FVD, and CLIPSIM are inconsistent with human judgment, and it proposes a hierarchical benchmark with separate dimensions for video quality and video-condition consistency [11].
citation_audit.evidence: The abstract/introduction says existing metrics such as Inception Score (IS), FID, FVD, and CLIPSIM are inconsistent with human judgement, and it says VBench uses a hierarchical and disentangled approach with two primary dimensions: Video Quality and Video-Condition Consistency.
